risks.risk: The CPU is not the claimed i7-9750H (could be a different model or generation)
risks.proof: A clear photo of the system information screen (e.g., Windows System Info or BIOS) showing the exact CPU model.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if it has a lower-end or different CPU, which may reduce value.

risks.risk: RAM is not 24GB (could be 16GB or less)
risks.proof: A photo of the system information screen showing installed RAM, or a photo of the RAM slots with installed sticks.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if it has 16GB RAM, which is less valuable than 24GB.

risks.risk: The laptop may have been modified or has hidden damage (e.g., cracked screen, liquid damage, non-original parts)
risks.proof: A full 360-degree video or close-up photos of the screen, hinges, ports, and underside for signs of damage or tampering.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if it has potential hidden damage, reducing value.

risks.risk: The GPU is not the claimed model (e.g., GTX 1660 Ti or RTX 2060, which are common in Helios 300 models)
risks.proof: A photo of the system information screen showing the exact GPU model.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if it has a lower-tier GPU, which may reduce value.

Close-up photo of the bottom label (on photo 1) to read the exact model number and serial.
Video or photos showing the laptop from all angles, including screen, ports, and hinges.
response.reason: The model is identifiable as Acer Predator Helios 300, but key specs like CPU, RAM, and GPU cannot be verified from the current photos. Without proof of these, the item cannot be priced accurately and risks being misvalued.
